title: Monkeys, Hamlet, and the Price of a Prompt: Language Models as Search-Space Compressors in Generate-and-Test Discovery
description: The infinite monkey theorem is true and useless: a million monkeys typing 2 keystrokes per second on a 27-key keyboard need an expected 10^186063 years to produce Hamlet, because blind sampling has neither a prior nor a verifier. Interposing a large language model between the monkeys and the page collapses the expected wait to 2,400 years for the prompt 'write hamlet' and to about three minutes for 'hamlet' -- a compression of roughly 10^186060 in expected time -- because training has already absorbed the target's improbability into the weights, leaving the monkeys to find only its ADDRESS. We work the arithmetic exactly (every number in this note is reproduced by a committed script, monkey_compression_check.py, published alongside), derive the informational floor on prompt length (the address cannot be shorter than the bits of the target NOT already in the model; prompt length is a measurement of how much of a target's description already resides in the machine, and 'fame' is exactly the shortness of an object's address), and then make the serious point the joke carries: the same two ingredients that rescue the monkeys -- a prior that proposes only well-formed candidates, and a verifier that scores each one against data -- convert blind exploration into feasible generate-and-test search, the blind-variation-plus-selective-retention algorithm of Campbell and Simon with the language model playing chemistry and the data playing selection. This is a legitimate discovery methodology with one non-negotiable caveat, stated at full weight: SEARCH-UNTIL-FIT GUARANTEES A FIT, so the fit that terminates a search is a selection event and never evidence; evidence is what the surviving candidate does on data it was never searched against, and the supporting discipline is pre-registration with frozen thresholds, committed runnable verification scripts for every load-bearing claim, and a public ledger of kills and retractions alongside survivors. A short case study describes the author's own use of the loop (exploratory LLM prompting filtered by scripted confrontation with public galaxy kinematics), cited strictly for its methodology ledger; this note takes no position on the correctness of any hypothesis so found. The limits of the analogy (non-uniform elicitation, copying-fidelity, verifier quality as the binding constraint, and the prior-as-cage regression toward the known) are stated. Conclusion: proposal has become nearly free; confirmation has not; that asymmetry is now the entire game.
notes: A methods essay, not a physics result. Every quantitative claim is reproduced by the committed script monkey_compression_check.py (exit 0), included in this record and at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula. The case study in Section 6 is cited for its methodology ledger (pre-registrations, verification scripts, retraction record), explicitly not as evidence for its physics claims.
